provenance.method: lesson notes written from the NERDC 2025 scheme of work outline; every week keeps its scheme topic and bullets as the teaching spine

topics.title: Democracy
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state the principles of democracy.
The students should be able to explain the practice of democracy in Nigeria.
Introduction:
We have learned about different types of government in our previous lessons. Today we will focus on democracy which is the type of government we have in Nigeria.
Content:
Democracy is government by the people for the people. The principles include free and fair elections, majority rule, minority rights, and protection of human rights. In Nigeria, we practice democracy through voting for leaders at local, state and federal levels. For example, during elections, Nigerians queue with their voters card to choose their leaders like the President, Governors and Local Government Chairmen.
Class activity:
Organize a mock election in the class where students will vote for their class captain following democratic principles.
Evaluation questions:
What is democracy?
List two principles of democracy.
How do Nigerians practice democracy?
Summary:
Democracy ensures that people have the power to choose their leaders through voting.

topics.title: Rule of law
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define the rule of law.
The students should be able to explain equality before the law.
Introduction:
Last week we discussed democracy where people vote for leaders. Today we will learn about rule of law which is important in a democratic society.
Content:
The rule of law means that everyone is equal before the law and no one is above the law. In Nigeria, from the President to a market woman in Onitsha, everyone must obey the law. For example, if someone steals from a market stall in Lagos, they will face the same legal process regardless of their position in society. This ensures justice and fairness for all citizens.
Class activity:
Case discussion - present a scenario where a rich person and a poor person commit the same offense and discuss how the law should apply equally to both.
Evaluation questions:
What is rule of law?
Explain equality before the law.
Give an example of rule of law in Nigeria.
Summary:
The rule of law ensures that everyone is treated equally and fairly by the legal system.

topics.title: Citizenship
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to list ways of acquiring citizenship.
The students should be able to explain the duties of a citizen.
Introduction:
We have learned about democracy and rule of law. Today we will discuss citizenship which is the status of being a member of a country.
Content:
Citizenship is the legal relationship between a person and a country. It can be acquired by birth, registration, naturalization or marriage. For example, a child born to Nigerian parents in Abuja is automatically a citizen. Duties of citizens include paying taxes, obeying laws, voting in elections, and defending the country. Like when adults pay their taxes to the government to build roads and schools.
Class activity:
Good citizen project - students create posters showing duties of a good Nigerian citizen.
Evaluation questions:
What is citizenship?
Name two ways of acquiring citizenship.
List three duties of a citizen.
Why is voting important for citizens?
Summary:
Citizenship comes with rights and responsibilities that help build a strong nation.

topics.title: Public service
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify different public servants.
The students should be able to explain the importance of honesty in public service.
Introduction:
After learning about citizenship, we now discuss public service which is how citizens contribute to national development.
Content:
Public service refers to services provided by the government for citizens. Public servants include teachers, doctors, police officers, civil servants and politicians. They work in offices like the Ministry of Education or local government secretariats. For example, a teacher in a public school is a public servant who helps educate children. Honesty is crucial in public service to prevent corruption like when a government official steals public money meant for building a community well.
Class activity:
Invite a local government worker to speak about their role and the importance of integrity in public service.
Evaluation questions:
Who is a public servant?
Give two examples of public servants in Nigeria.
Why is honesty important in public service?
What happens when public servants are not honest?
Summary:
Public servants work for the benefit of all citizens and must serve with integrity.

topics.title: Drug abuse
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify common abused drugs.
The students should be able to explain the social effects of drug abuse.
Introduction:
We have discussed how citizens contribute to society through public service. Today we will learn about drug abuse which is a serious problem affecting our communities.
Content:
Drug abuse is the misuse of drugs for non-medical purposes. Common abused drugs include marijuana (Indian hemp), codeine, tramadol and cocaine. The social effects include increased crime rates, family breakdown, health problems and reduced productivity. For example, a person who abuses drugs might steal from neighbors to buy more drugs or neglect their family responsibilities. In Nigeria, we see this problem in some areas where young men who abuse hemp become violent and disturb the peace.
Class activity:
Prevention campaign - students create short dramas or posters warning about the dangers of drug abuse.
Evaluation questions:
What is drug abuse?
Name two commonly abused drugs in Nigeria.
Explain two social effects of drug abuse.
How can drug abuse affect a student's education?
Summary:
Drug abuse has serious negative effects on individuals, families and society.

topics.title: Human trafficking
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define human trafficking.
The students should be able to explain dangers and prevention methods.
Introduction:
We discussed drug abuse last week. Today we will learn about human trafficking which is another serious social problem affecting our country.
Content:
Human trafficking is the illegal trade of humans for forced labor, sexual exploitation or organ removal. In Nigeria, many young people are promised good jobs abroad but end up being enslaved. Dangers include physical abuse, emotional trauma, loss of freedom and death. For example, some girls from Edo State are trafficked to Europe with false promises of jobs but end up as sex workers. Prevention involves community awareness, education and strict law enforcement.
Class activity:
Students create awareness posters about human trafficking and how to protect themselves and others.
Evaluation questions:
What is human trafficking?
Name two dangers of human trafficking.
How can human trafficking affect families?
What can communities do to prevent human trafficking?
Summary:
Human trafficking is a crime that exploits vulnerable people and must be prevented through awareness and law enforcement.

topics.title: Cultism
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to define cultism.
The students should be able to explain the dangers of cultism to youth.
Introduction:
After learning about human trafficking, we now discuss cultism which is another serious social issue affecting young people in Nigeria.
Content:
Cultism is the practice of joining secret societies with oaths and rituals that often involve violence. In Nigerian schools, cult groups like Vikings and Buccaneers recruit students with promises of protection and belonging. Dangers to youth include physical harm, academic failure, criminal records and death. For example, some university students have been killed during cult clashes on campus. Youth should choose wisely and focus on their education instead of joining such groups.
Class activity:
Role play - students demonstrate how to say no to cult recruitment and report such activities to authorities.
Evaluation questions:
What is cultism?
Name two dangers of cultism to students.
How can cultism affect a student's future?
What should students do if approached by cult groups?
Summary:
Cultism destroys lives and futures; students should avoid it and focus on positive activities.

topics.title: HIV and society
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to state facts about HIV.
The students should be able to explain how society should care for people living with HIV.
Introduction:
We have discussed social problems like cultism. Today we will learn about HIV and how society should respond to it.
Content:
HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and can lead to AIDS if not treated. Facts about HIV include: it is spread through specific body fluids, not through casual contact, and can be managed with medication. In Nigeria, many people living with HIV face stigma and discrimination. Society should care for them without stigma, just like we care for people with other illnesses. For example, a neighbor with HIV should not be avoided but supported to take their medication regularly.
Class activity:
No stigma campaign - students create posters promoting acceptance and support for people living with HIV.
Evaluation questions:
What is HIV?
How is HIV transmitted?
Why is stigma harmful to people living with HIV?
How can society support people living with HIV?
Summary:
HIV can be managed with proper care and acceptance without stigma.

topics.title: Environmental problems
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to identify environmental problems in Nigeria.
The students should be able to suggest local solutions to environmental problems.
Introduction:
We have discussed social issues affecting people. Today we will focus on environmental problems that affect our communities and health.
Content:
Environmental problems in Nigeria include erosion, flooding, pollution and deforestation. Gully erosion in places like Anambra State destroys farmland and houses. Flooding in Lagos during rainy seasons displaces families and damages property. Pollution from industries and improper waste disposal affects air and water quality. Local solutions include planting trees to prevent erosion, building proper drainage systems, and proper waste management. For example, communities can organize monthly cleaning exercises to reduce pollution.
Class activity:
Students identify an environmental problem in their community and propose solutions in a short presentation.
Evaluation questions:
Name two environmental problems in Nigeria.
How does erosion affect communities?
What causes flooding in Nigerian cities?
What local solutions can help reduce pollution?
Summary:
Environmental problems require community action and sustainable practices for a healthier environment.

topics.title: Revision and BECE practice
topics.content:
Behavioural objectives:
The students should be able to answer past BECE questions correctly.
The students should be able to identify areas needing further study.
Introduction:
This is our last week of term. We will revise what we have learned and practice questions similar to the BECE examination.
Content:
We will review topics covered this term including democracy, rule of law, citizenship, public service, drug abuse, human trafficking, cultism, HIV and environmental problems. Students will attempt past BECE Social Studies questions. We will mark the questions together and discuss areas where students made mistakes. For example, questions about principles of democracy or duties of citizens often appear in the exam and require clear understanding.
Class activity:
Group work - students work in teams to solve past BECE questions and present their answers to the class.
Evaluation questions:
What is the difference between democracy and rule of law?
Explain two duties of a Nigerian citizen.
What are the dangers of cultism?
How can we prevent environmental problems in our community?
Summary:
Revision helps reinforce learning and prepare students for the BECE examination.
